function: Learned (AE plus RNN) prediction of significant delay-Doppler-angle CSI elements for MIMO-OTFS, then LS channel estimation with a new pilot structure (pp. 1-2, 6-9).
system: MIMO-OTFS downlink: base station ULA with M=32 antennas, one single-antenna high-mobility user, 30 GHz carrier, 125 MHz bandwidth, 4-QAM; no RIS (pp. 3, 11).
method: Auto-encoder (3-D CNN) compresses CSI; one-hidden-layer RNN predicts it; AE decoder gives significant-element indices; LS re-estimates values; AE trained by MSE reconstruction, RNN on channel samples (pp. 6-8, 11).
data_channel: Own simulated multipath channel at 30 GHz: 50 clusters of 10 static scatters, uniform cluster centres, 30 m coverage; cluster idea cites COST 2100 [36] (p. 11).
test_conditions: AE: 100K random CSIs (90K/10K split); RNN: 40 trajectories on a 20 m by 10 m track; tested at 25, 50, 100 m/s, training velocity not stated (p. 11).
baselines: Non-learned: PAD prediction [14], OMP estimation [45], traditional LS pilot, perfect CSI as BER reference; no learned baseline (pp. 11-12).
metrics: NMSE of predicted and estimated channel; BER of message-passing detection; ratios of missed and added significant elements; parameters, FLOPs, computing time (pp. 11-12).
complexity: Order O(l_max d_max M); AE 136,000 parameters, 1,280 MFLOPs, 38 us; RNN 2,097,152 parameters, 8.3 MFLOPs, 0.246 us (Table IV, p. 12).
q1_support: p. 11: "the individual reflection angles of the scatters are the same as the corresponding cluster angle [36]". The simulator is the authors' own cluster model (50 clusters, 10 static scatters each, 30 GHz); [36] (COST 2100, p. 13) is cited only for the cluster idea (pp. 3, 11) and the text never says the simulator is built on COST 2100.
q2_support: p. 11: "different velocities are tested, e.g., 100 m/s, 50 m/s and 25 m/s" but the training velocity is not stated; the AE data are "randomly generated in an arbitrary environment with parameters in Table II" (which lists 25, 50, 100 m/s) and the RNN is trained on the target track, so no condition unseen in training is reported.
q3_support: p. 12: "The proposed scheme is compared with an existing channel prediction scheme [14] and an OMP based estimation scheme [45]." Both are non-learned (Prony-based PAD and OMP) and the traditional LS pilot is also classical; no earlier learned predictor or standard network (LSTM, GRU, CNN) is compared.
q4_support: p. 12: "the proposed scheme has a linear complexity order denoted as" O(l_max d_max M), with the FLOPs formula (42) and Table IV (AE 136,000 parameters, 1,280 MFLOPs, 38 us; RNN 2,097,152 parameters, 8.3 MFLOPs, 0.246 us).
q5_support: p. 11: "We first generate dataset to train the AE network" (own simulated CSI, 100K samples); no code or data link, DOI, or public dataset is given anywhere in the paper.
notes: PDF title (p. 1) is 'Deep Learning Supported Path Prediction and Channel Estimation for MIMO-OTFS System With High Delay Resolution' and the DOI printed on p. 1 matches. Area 4 (delay-Doppler channel prediction and estimation for OTFS) wins over area 2. The learned part is the AE-RNN prediction of significant elements (pp. 6-8); LS estimation and message-passing detection are classical. Borderline for the reviewer: q1 is 0 because the text never says its simulator is COST 2100 although [36], the COST 2100 paper, is cited for clusters (pp. 3, 11); q2 is 0 because the training velocity is not stated for the 25/50/100 m/s tests. Centre frequency 30 GHz (p. 11).
